analysis.one_liner: Trent runs Tata Group's retail chains - Westside (fashion department stores), Zudio (value fashion) and Star Bazaar (grocery) - and is best known for Zudio's rapid store rollout.
analysis.whats_happening: Trent reported Q2 FY27 results on 29 October 2026: consolidated revenue of ₹5,873 crore (up 22% YoY), EBITDA of ₹785 crore (up 37%) and PAT of ₹468 crore (up 25%). During the quarter Zudio crossed 1,000 stores (including 7 in the UAE), Westside added stores to reach 311, and Star Bazaar grew revenue over 20% to 87 stores. This followed a weaker Q1 FY27 (revenue up only 19% against a ~22% street estimate), which had triggered a sharp single-day stock fall on growth-deceleration worries.
analysis.plain_terms: Trent is a retail growth story: it keeps opening Zudio stores at a fast clip and that drives most of the revenue increase. The tension beginners should understand is that the stock has fallen hard from its 2024 peak because the market is questioning whether each new store is producing as much sales per square foot as before - fast store count growth is not the same as fast per-store growth, and investors have started pricing in the difference.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 missed growth expectations (revenue +19% vs ~22% expected) and the stock fell sharply on the day. Q2 FY27 bounced back with revenue +22% YoY, EBITDA +37% and consolidated PAT +25%, with EBITDA margin improving to 11.6%. H1 FY27 overall: revenue +20%, EBITDA +35%, PAT +24%. One caveat: standalone PAT growth for the quarter was reported inconsistently across sources (figures ranging from roughly 9% to 25% YoY), so the consolidated numbers above are the ones to rely on. Specific same-store-sales growth figures for Zudio and Westside this quarter were not disclosed in sources checked - not verified.
analysis.performance_read: Per the verified data, the stock is down 36.3% over one year versus a 10.9% fall in the Nifty, but up 40.4% over three years and 195.8% over five years, both well ahead of the index. It remains 63.3% below its October 2024 peak of ₹8,218, despite trading at ₹3,017 now versus a 52-week low of ₹2,194. This is a genuine valuation correction and growth-deceleration story, not a corporate-action artifact - the company did carry out a 1:2 bonus issue in June 2026, but the price and dividend history used here is already adjusted for that, so the drawdown figure is real, not inflated by an unadjusted bonus.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 85x trailing earnings and about 20x book value, Trent is still priced for sustained high growth even after a 63% fall from its peak. It is expensive because the market has historically paid up for Zudio's expansion story and Trent's unusually high returns on capital; whether that premium is justified now hinges entirely on whether the Q1 FY27 growth miss was a one-off or the start of a structural slowdown in store productivity - the Q2 bounce-back argues for the former, but one strong quarter doesn't settle it.
analysis.growth_read: Growth continues to be driven mainly by adding stores - Zudio alone crossed the 1,000-store mark this quarter - rather than purely by existing stores selling more, which is why a single quarter of slower store-count-adjusted growth (Q1 FY27) was enough to spook the market. The 37% EBITDA growth this quarter, ahead of 22% revenue growth, shows margins are improving as the business scales, so it's volume-led growth with a margin tailwind rather than margin-led growth on a flat store base.
analysis.health_read: The balance sheet is clean: Trent is in a net cash position with debt-to-equity near 0.3x (including lease liabilities), and returns on capital remain strong (ROE ~27.7%, ROCE ~28.3%). No red flags on profit-to-cash conversion were found. The real question for Trent is business risk - whether store-level growth can keep pace with expectations in a competitive value-fashion market - not financial or balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Tata Sons at ~32.5% and Tata Investment Corporation at ~4.3%, totalling ~37%) hold no pledged shares. FIIs hold about 15.3% and domestic institutions about 23.3%. No specific marquee individual or boutique investor was found on the shareholder register in sources checked - if you were expecting a well-known name here, none turned up.
strengths: Zudio crossed 1,000 stores in Q2 FY27, showing the format can scale fast across geographies
EBITDA grew 37% YoY against 22% revenue growth, lifting margin to 11.6%
ROE of ~27.7% and ROCE of ~28.3% alongside a net-cash balance sheet (debt-to-equity ~0.3x)
Promoter holding of ~37% with zero pledge, signalling no financial stress at the promoter level
watchpoints: Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 19% missed street estimates of ~22% and triggered a sharp stock fall - a sign that per-store productivity may be softening even as store count keeps rising
At ~85x earnings, the stock still prices in high sustained growth; further growth misses could extend the de-rating already seen since the October 2024 peak
Same-store-sales growth figures for Zudio and Westside were not clearly disclosed this quarter - not verified, and this is the key number markets are watching for
The stock remains 63% below its 2024 peak even after a recovery from 52-week lows, reflecting an unresolved debate about the sustainability of Zudio's growth rate
analysis.one_thing: Same-store-sales growth for Zudio in the next quarter (Q3 FY27, expected mid-to-late January 2027) - a stabilising or reaccelerating number would support the view that Q1 FY27's miss was temporary, while continued softness would validate the market's post-2024 de-rating.
analysis.data_notes: Price, return and drawdown figures are taken from the verified market data feed and not recomputed. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT figures were cross-checked across multiple reports of the 29 October 2026 results and are consistent; the standalone PAT YoY growth percentage varied across sources and was therefore not used. ROCE was reported as both ~28.3% and ~36.7% in different sources - the lower, more conservative figure is used here. Specific SSSG percentages for Zudio/Westside this quarter could not be verified - check latest investor presentation on the company's website or Screener for confirmation.
